name: Shakti OBE: chirp, right hemisphere
origin: Todd Murphy, 8 Coil Shakti OBE recipe
summary: An OBE session for the 8 Coil Shakti with the chirp signal: 30 min over the right hemisphere, then sleep about an hour later. Murphy lists the chirp as one of three candidate signals, calls it an untested signal and warns that it can be very unpleasant over the right side. No user report ties it to an OBE, and the 30 min are this project's choice.
setting: Lie down in a dark, quiet room. Murphy reports that most OBEs came when users fell asleep about 1 h (or 90 min) after a session, so plan to go to sleep then and use your OBE exercises; he expects it to work more often in 'right-hemispheric' people.
schedule: Vendor rules: at most once a week or every 72 h, never on consecutive days; a series of up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break. No more than two series over the right angular gyrus; after that, choose another session design.
notes: The vendor suggests 'sessions over the right hemisphere (temporal lobes, parietal lobes or the area behind the parietal lobes)' with the hippocampal signals, the modulated 40 hertz signal or the chirp (shakti_obe.htm). Its angular-gyrus page does not name the chirp, and no OBE page gives a length. This program plays 30 min on six coils together: FT10 and T10 in front of and below the right ear, TP8, CP6, P6 and P8 around the right angular gyrus; two channels stay silent. The length, the six coils and the sites are this project's choices. The two spots come from a two-coil placement the vendor gives for the modulated 40 Hz signal only (obe45_consent.htm). The vendor builds its chirp from frequency-modulated gaps and Fibonacci-stepped amplitudes (mod40_chirp_consent.htm, TECHNICAL INFORMATION); the file is not published. The stand-in here is this project's plain sweep, falling from 40 to 6 Hz in 2.5 s, then 1.5 s off, on 3-ms points; it does not reproduce that build. Field strength: this program's sources state none. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. No source links the chirp to an OBE. The vendor says it 'should be considered an untested signal' and suggests 'that you not use it by itself until after you have used Shakti in other ways' (mod40_chirp_consent.htm). Blanke et al. 2002 evoked an OBE at the right angular gyrus with implanted electrodes; weak-field effects there are untested. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The vendor warns that the chirp 'can be very unpleasant over the right side': stop if fear comes; it is no endurance test. Word-finding trouble means stop using the signal (vendor). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop at once on fear or any distress.
